timer.preset.classic.name: Pomodoro
timer.preset.classic.note: Francesco Cirillo's Pomodoro Technique. In a 2023 study, students who took fixed breaks like these reported less fatigue and more concentration and motivation than students who took breaks whenever they chose.
timer.preset.deep.name: Deep work
timer.preset.deep.note: A longer variant for work that takes a while to get into. Not studied directly; it keeps the key ingredient: breaks on a fixed schedule instead of when you are already drained.
timer.preset.desktime.note: From DeskTime's tracking data on its most productive users. Observational company data, not a controlled study, so treat it as a starting point to adjust.
timer.preset.ultradian.name: Ultradian
timer.preset.ultradian.note: Built around ~90-minute ultradian cycles (the basic rest–activity cycle). Plausible for long creative work, but evidence that daytime attention follows a strict 90-minute rhythm is weak.
timer.preset.custom.name: Custom schedule
timer.preset.custom.note: Your own lengths. Whatever they are, keep breaks regular: brief planned diversions keep attention from fading over long tasks.
timer.breaks.note: Make breaks real breaks: step away from the screen, move, and look into the distance.
sound.title: Focus sound
sound.status.preview: Preview · stops when you close this panel
sound.status.waiting: Plays while a focus session runs
sound.status.failed: Could not open the audio output
sound.custom.note: Your own mix of noise and tones. Pick a preset to see the research behind it.
preset.speech.name: Speech masking
preset.speech.note: Pink noise covers nearby conversation, the sound that disrupts reading and writing the most (the irrelevant speech effect). Its energy falls with frequency, so it sounds softer and less hissy than white noise.
preset.white.name: Attention boost
preset.white.note: Background white noise improved memory in inattentive and ADHD children (the moderate brain arousal model), but slightly hurt children who were already attentive. Test it on yourself.
preset.brown.name: Deep brown
preset.brown.note: A deep, soft rumble. It masks sound the same way with far less high-frequency hiss, so many find it easier to bear for hours. Very popular, but there is little direct research on brown noise and focus.
preset.beta.name: Beta vigilance
preset.beta.note: 16 Hz binaural beats in pink noise improved vigilance and mood compared with slow 1.5–4 Hz beats. A small study. Needs headphones.
preset.gamma.name: Gamma attention
preset.gamma.note: 40 Hz binaural beats reduced the attentional blink (missing a second target right after a first), but only in some people, depending on their dopamine levels. Needs headphones.
preset.alpha.name: Alpha calm
preset.alpha.note: 10 Hz beats over brown noise for relaxed alertness, good for settling in before work. A meta-analysis found binaural beats can help memory, attention and anxiety, with large differences between studies. Needs headphones.
preset.iso40.name: 40 Hz pulses
preset.iso40.note: Pulsed 40 Hz tones that work on speakers. Based on 40 Hz sensory stimulation (GENUS) research, which is promising in mice; cognitive benefits in healthy people are unproven.
noise.note: Equal sliders are pink noise. For less hiss, lower the highs or add softness; to cover voices, keep 500 Hz–4 kHz up (ANSI S3.5). Width: wider sounds more spacious, mono sits inside your head.
tune.eq.hint: Drag a band to shape it
tone.note: Whether beats entrain brainwaves is debated; keep the tone only if it helps you.
tone.note.binaural: Binaural beats need headphones. Whether beats entrain brainwaves is debated; keep the tone only if it helps you.
alerts.barTime: Show the time in the bar
alerts.note: Different sounds for the end of focus and the end of a break let you tell them apart without looking.
